name: Emergency Rescue: Critical Crisis of Respiratory Failure
description: In the early morning hours, the elderly patient in bed 36, who had a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease combined with coronary heart disease, suddenly experienced shortness of breath, restlessness, and a sharp drop in blood oxygen saturation to 85%. Yu Xiaowen’s heart tightened, and she immediately rushed to the bedside, instructing the nurse: "High-flow oxygen via mask, prepare for ECG monitoring, and draw arterial blood gas!" While quickly performing a lung auscultation (wheezing and moist rales were heard throughout), she used the duty phone to call Dr. Li Wei. Over the phone, she clearly reported the patient’s condition. Dr. Li Wei instructed her to immediately administer intravenous methylprednisolone and anti-asthmatic medication, and to prepare for non-invasive ventilator-assisted ventilation if necessary. Yu Xiaowen calmly issued the medical orders, directed the nurses to carry them out, and stayed by the bedside to closely monitor the patient’s response. After nearly an hour of intense and orderly rescue efforts, the patient’s breathing gradually stabilized, and their blood oxygen level rose to 92%, temporarily stabilizing their condition. Only then did she realize that the back of her scrubs was soaked with cold sweat.

name: Financial Review and Asset Adjustment Planning
description: Commence execution of today's core task. Log into banking and fund platforms one by one, and create a detailed table listing the current market values and profit/loss status of all demand deposits, time deposits, and various types of funds held (money market, bond, hybrid, equity). The data clearly shows that high-risk (equity) funds account for over 80%, which is severely misaligned with her current situation of facing rental changes and needing a stronger financial safety net. She has identified the core adjustment goal: systematically reduce the proportion of high-risk assets and enhance the defensive nature of the investment portfolio. Between 10:45 and 11:00, she got up to move around, made a cup of chrysanthemum tea, checked her phone, replied to a colleague Wang Fang from her department regarding a patient's medication inquiry, and reviewed a link to the latest literature shared by her mentor Li Wei in the group chat. This brief shift in attention allowed her mind to relax. Subsequently, based on yesterday's communication with financial advisor Wang Mingyuan and the organized data, she began formulating a specific and actionable plan. Decision: Starting from April 2025, after each monthly salary is deposited, a fixed 30% will be allocated to selected money market funds and pure bond funds, achieving the dual purposes of "forced savings" and "risk hedging." She meticulously planned the fixed investment dates, amounts, and alternative fund products, and compiled the entire thought process, adjustment rationale, and operational steps into a clear electronic document, ready to be sent to Manager Wang next week for final confirmation. After completing this complex planning, she let out a long sigh of relief, and a sense of steadiness from regaining control over her life emerged.

After arriving home, I first placed the Monstera plant by the window in the living room to add a touch of greenery. I trimmed the sunflowers and arranged them in a vase, placing it on the dining table. Next, I started unpacking the remaining boxes in the bedroom, mainly containing clothes and bedding, and began sorting and organizing them. At the same time, I used a food delivery app on my phone to order dinner—a half-and-half pizza and a salad.  

At 18:00, my close friend Zhang Jing arrived right on time, bringing a bottle of fruit wine as a "housewarming gift." After hugging, we immediately dove into the organizing. I was in charge of deciding where things should go and how to arrange them, while Zhang Jing helped by passing items, wiping surfaces, and assembling simple furniture. We focused on tackling the clutter in the kitchen and bedroom, chatting as we worked—about today’s farewell, our feelings about the new home, and the interesting things that had happened to us over the week.  

At 19:30, the food delivery arrived. We paused our organizing to enjoy the pizza and salad at the dining table, toasting to the new home and shifting our conversation from work to life. After dinner at 20:30, we gathered our momentum and cleared away all the scattered packaging materials, swept the floor, and bagged up the trash.  

By 21:30, the organizing was mostly done. We settled on the sofa to relax, playing soothing classical music while continuing our casual chat and planning to watch a movie together next week.  

At 22:00, Zhang Jing prepared to leave. I walked her to the elevator, thanking her once again for her help and company.

However, during shaping and texture imprinting, the clay repeatedly deformed and cracked at the edges. After multiple failed attempts, I felt extremely frustrated. After class, instead of directly instructing on techniques, Teacher Zheng Guodong guided Yu Xiaowen to reflect on her experiences in hospital work regarding the fragility and resilience of life. He offered insight, saying, "Clay has life too. You’re too focused on controlling its perfect ‘form,’ forgetting to feel the ‘state’ it wants to express. Try channeling the feelings you have in the hospital into the strength of your hands and the patterns in your heart." These words brought her a sudden realization that pottery serves as a medium for expressing inner emotions. Seizing the moment of inspiration, she immediately used her phone’s memo app in a corner of the studio to jot down keywords like "pulse texture" and "layered time," and sketched abstract designs.

I explained the printing requirements in detail to the staff: A4 matte coated paper, color printing, and perfect binding. While waiting for the binding, I double-checked the layout and content on my phone. Once bound into a booklet, I was pleased with its sturdy feel and clear text and images. I then went next door to the "Cainiao Post" courier point, carefully wrapping the handbook in bubble wrap and placing it in a cardboard box. I added a handwritten note: "Mom and Dad, your little health guide is ready! I hope you like it, and even more, I hope you use it often. Love, Wenwen."
